title: Amulets
subtitle: It's time to leave—ready or not.

items.text: Amulets
A door opens.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *pant*
Then another, as if by divine intervention.
Fourth Floor, Central Watchtower

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: It's been a little too easy. Don't you think? It's like someone's walking ahead and unlocking all the doors for us.
As if by way of reply, the next door opens to greet them.
Clearly unsettled, Lucas huddles up to Emilia to whisper into her ear.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: You think it's ghosts?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Ah! D-Don't be ridiculous. And even if there were ghosts, they'd obviously be haunting the detention room.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It couldn't be. The school hires exorcists for a full inspection every vernal equinox. Didn't you know that?
The attempt to calm their fears falls flat. Assurances of safety do little in the face of the crisis around them.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But if you're still worried, I've got just the thing for you two.
She reaches into her pocket.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Here. Keep these close.
Cold, hard metal sits in their palms.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: I thought you were going to give us a talisman or an amulet to keep the ghosts away.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Well, these are pretty much the same thing.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Lucas, yours has got an optical incantation that can make you invisible.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But yours, Emilia, is a real-live grenade. Throw it out, and it'll set off a small explosion, understand? I bet the instructors never let you try these before. Pretty cool, right?

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Yeah, sure, but why does she get the real thing?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Because as far as I've seen, Emilia thinks before she acts. I can trust her to use it responsibly.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You, on the other hand, would probably lob it out the first chance you got.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: I would not.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: I'll be careful. I promise.
Her voice is so low it's as if she's speaking to herself.
Merel ruffles the hair of her two young friends and then turns to make for the stairs.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Alright then. Let's keep moving.
The staircase's spiral rise blurs the trio's perception. It feels as if each turn should be the last, and yet it continues onward until the climb becomes almost excruciating.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: The top floor is right above us.
Emilia pauses before the window ahead, perhaps too narrow for an intruder to get through, but wide enough to make them visible to enemy eyes.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Watch out!
She stumbles back, but Merel's outstretched hand grabs hers before she can tumble backward.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Emilia? What is it? You're shaking.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Look. Over there.
The exterior walls of the SPDM have melted like candlewax. Bloodstains and rust mar the once-pristine, indestructible barriers. Sparks dance along the ground, igniting the grass into growing flames.
The "Storm" is crossing over the now-unprotected campus. Clashing eras warp the outer buildings as the architecture shifts rapidly between different shapes and styles.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: We'll be okay.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin's doing everything she can. So, we've got to do the same.
Her pounding heart feels as if it is lodged in her throat as she taps on the locked door.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Vertin, Sonetto, is this you helping us?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I don't know how you're doing this. But if it really is you, then please, we need your help one last time.
As if answering her plea, the door opens. Behind it lies darkness—an unpredictable black hole.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: The door's open, again.
Merel grasps the children's hands, trying to mask the trembling in her own.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The thing we're after should be right behind it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That was the last knot.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: If all the knots are undone, will Merel be able to get to the top floor safely?
A jumble of golden thread that's accumulated halfway in pushes through to the darkness beyond the door.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think so.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then she'll be able to get the Dove to the library. I know she will. Let's head back and meet her there.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But first, we need to find a way out.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper?
Before Sonetto, a pair of sightless eyes stare off in another direction.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Which way am I facing, Sonetto? What's in this direction?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's a door. Shall I open it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, please. And tell me what's behind it.
She comes to a sudden halt.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is there something wrong, Sonetto?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It opens into another space. If I'm not mistaken ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's the Committee Building's hallway.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then this maze can lead us to Foundation headquarters.
More golden threads sprawl out, but none glow like Merel's did. These new lines are faint, as if drifting between the destined and the uncertain.
Something in this chaotic darkness is pursuing the strings, causing them to tangle along their original paths. Then the darkness takes shape.
The shadow flickers. Each time it appears, it feels as if it siphons the air from the lungs.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's Arcana. She's here.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Arcana?
Sonetto can't see anything in the empty hall around them.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You mean, at the school? Or at headquarters?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At headquarters, inside the Committee Building. I think I know why the Foundation never sent more reinforcements to the school.
